name: sector_pair_reversion_v1
author: quant_system
thesis: Cointegrated pairs within the same sector (e.g., HDFC Bank vs ICICI Bank, TCS vs Infosys) exhibit intraday spread mean-reversion because they share common fundamental drivers. When the spread deviates, it's usually due to temporary order flow imbalance (one stock getting a large block, the other not yet). The inefficiency exists because intraday spread monitoring requires real-time cointegration tracking. Not fully arbitraged because the spread can remain dislocated for hours and sizing is constrained by single-name liquidity.
stock_filter: pre-selected cointegrated pairs: (HDFCBANK, ICICIBANK), (TCS, INFY), (RELIANCE, BHARTIARTL), (SBIN, BANKBARODA), (MARUTI, M&M)

entry.entry_price: market on confirmation — simultaneously enter both legs

exit.trailing_stop: none — target is mean reversion of spread

risk.position_sizing: hedge_ratio_adjusted — size legs by hedge ratio

filters.time_filter: no trades first 15 min or last 20 min
filters.volume_filter: both legs must have volume > 70% of 20-bar avg
filters.spread_filter: skip if either leg has spread > 0.1%
filters.event_filter: skip if either stock has earnings within 3 days
other_filters: re-estimate hedge ratio weekly using 60-day rolling OLS

edge.edge_decay_risk: medium — structural (sector cointegration) but pairs break down

weaknesses: Cointegration breaks down. Pairs that were cointegrated last quarter may not be this quarter. SBIN/BANKBARODA in particular has unstable hedge ratios.
Double the transaction costs — you're paying brokerage, STT, slippage on BOTH legs. The 22 bps edge needs to cover ~18-20 bps in round-trip costs for TWO stocks.
Execution risk: you need simultaneous fills on both legs. If one leg fills and the other moves, you have unwanted directional exposure.
prior_art: Classic pairs trading. See: Algorithmic Trading (Chan), Gatev/Goetzmann/Rouwenhorst (2006). Intraday adaptation.
notes: Run Engle-Granger cointegration test weekly. Drop any pair with p-value > 0.05. Keep a spare pair list to rotate in.
